headline: Discussed Natural Resource Overlay District zoning changes, comp plan resiliency priorities, and Conservation Legacy Fund grant program
summary: The board discussed draft Natural Resource Overlay District zoning amendments for rare, threatened, and endangered species and Tier 1a status. Members also generated a list of resiliency priorities for the Comprehensive Plan and heard an update on the Conservation Legacy Fund grant program, including a $8,000 neighborhood plant pilot project. The August 3, 2026 minutes were postponed due to lack of a quorum.
decisions: Postponed approval of the August 3, 2026 minutes due to lack of a quorum.

Conservation Board Meeting Minutes 
Monday, October 5, 2026 – 5:30 pm 
In-Person Meeting 
 
Attendance   
 Board Members: Rebecca Roman (RR), Dale Azaria (DA), Lee Toomey (LT) 
 Absent: Zoe Richards (ZR), Alan Reichard (AR), Ryan Crehan (RC), Kelly Farrell (KF), Evan Horne 
(EH) 
 Public: August Talamadge, Sharon Bushor (phone) 
 Staff: Dan Cahill (Parks & Rec), Sarah Morgan (City Planning) 
 
RR, chair, called the meeting to order at 5:39 p.m.  
 
Minutes 
 
August 3, 2026 minutes 
 
Postponed due to lack of a quorum. 
 
Board Comment 
 
None. 
 
Public Comment 
 
August Talamadge, staffer from VYCC, spoke on behalf of VYCC conservation crews. 
 
Sharon Bushor commented as to resiliency.  Value and role the urban forest and trees play in keeping 
this section of the planet livable are spot on. The question asking about our climate vulnerabilities brings 
to mind drought, warming temperatures and unpredictable seasonal temperatures.  How to sustain and 
grow our urban forest brings to mind minimal human-controlled intervention into the natural process of 
tree decomposition and what this process sustains. Preservation of small groves of trees like the Silver 
Maples in the Intervale are another example. 
 
Update & Discussion 
 
1. Natural Resource Overlay District Zoning Amendment 
Consideration of draft changes to include provisions for rare, threatened, and endangered species 
 
Sarah Morgan from City Planning attended to present on the Natural Resource District Zoning 
Amendment.  Burlington is seeking Tier1a status for specific areas in the City identified as growth areas.   
 
The amendments are intended to decrease duplication of state and local permit and development 
processes.
Conservation Board Minutes 
October 5, 2026 - pg. 2 
   
Questions were asked about the difference between a field visit and field verification as well as the vetting 
process when applicants are being required to provide field verification, inventory, and assessment. 
 
DA shared that Burlington doesn’t have to follow the ACT250 standard only.  We can adopt our specific 
framework to be whatever we want. 
 
Sarah shared that currently Burlington is not looking to extend beyond aligning with State standards.  
 
Discussion ensued to determine what is considered in the 10-acre minimum. 
 
Sarah, we may need to define project as to determining the applicability of 10 acres. 
 
Dan Cahill asked where to find the map that shows where the Tier 1A applicable areas  are. 
 
2. Conservation Board Resiliency Priorities for the Comprehensive Plan 
Discussion and identification of resiliency priorities to include in the Comp Plan 
 
The board members present generated the following list of potential resiliency priorities:  
● Raw sewage in the lake; waste water management 
● ONE has less trees and green spaces and parks and gardens  
● South end has less community gardens 
● Use of the Urban Reserve  
● Re-naturalize the shoreline of the Urban Reserve 
● Building and infrastructure within shoreline, floodplain, and wetlands  
● Permanent protections for our public open spaces  
● Impervious surfaces, and surface runoff  
● Increasing stormwater management minimums for developments  
● More walkability, bike access, and bus infrastructure - reducing reliance on cars  
● Stewardship Zones - as defined and outlined in the Open Space Plan  
● Sustainably integrated local food systems in Burlington proper  
● Permanent infrastructure for farmer’s market? 
● Edible food forest  
● Deer management  
● Old housing stock and higher energy use needed for the extreme temperatures  
● Re-emphasize the amount of work that went into the OSP and what a high quality product it is  
● The comp plan should start THERE!! We are generating some specific ideas, but GO TO 
THE OPEN SPACE PLAN. Everything we need to say is IN THAT PLAN.  
3. Conservation Legacy Fund Grant Application  
Updates & pilot program for the upcoming grant program 
 
Dan Cahill said he’d send a Doodle poll to the review committee in order to set January application review 
dates.  Up to $8,000 will be set aside for the neighborhood plant pilot project.   
 
Adjournment 
7:27 PM.
